reasoning_traces.think:
The commonality index (CI) operates as a normalized measure of shared customer engagement between two items. It is defined by the ratio of intersecting customer sets to the geometric mean of individual item customer bases. This formulation ensures that items with high overlap but low absolute popularity do not dominate comparisons with more popular items having fewer overlaps. The asymmetrical variant adjusts this by weighting only the denominator, reflecting how much of one item’s customer base also engages with another. Sorting these indices allows rapid access to most similar items, enabling scalable recommendation systems. Failure modes include division by zero when item populations are empty, or misinterpretation of sparse data leading to spurious similarities. The symmetry property simplifies computation but may overlook nuanced directional preferences.
